findings.title: The next question becomes a procedural boundary
findings.claim: The conditional next question turns repeated failure into a self-imposed procedural endpoint: once a sufficient excuse is reached, ending the companionship becomes accountable rather than arbitrary.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers بَلَغْتَ and عُذْرًا join reaching a completion point with a ground that removes blame, while the supplied wider completion and withdrawal contacts return through the focus condition and companionship relation. The next question therefore changes the status of the relationship.
findings.reader_payoff: The final clause becomes a rule being fulfilled: the learner's repeated breach has produced a point at which separation can be justified.
findings.containment: This adds procedural accountability to the plain request to end companionship; it does not replace that request, make every question relationship-ending, or assert a legal verdict beyond the supplied relation.

epistemic.reason: The citable cross-run support directly anchors the focus occurrences and all three supplied branches; the connection rows provide wider corroborating contacts without turning their retrieval labels into a ranking.

findings.title: Companionship has terms
findings.claim: The focus's prohibition on companionship can be read as a rule-specific boundary on a close relation: the relationship changes when its stated learning condition is breached, even though companionship elsewhere can remain while a prohibited demand is refused.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the separation as a precise change in the terms of one relation, with the broader value of companionship still visible around it.
findings.containment: This does not import the full family-duty setting of 31:15, claim that every disobedient request ends companionship, or displace the focus's direct conditional statement.
